readmeHtml:
Orchestrator.inc

Stop babysitting agents. Start merging real work.

Run a fleet of coding agents while keeping branches, reviews, and CI failures manageable.


Get Orchestrator.inc  •  Documentation  •  Releases  •  Contributing  •  Discord

English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Español · Français · Deutsch · Português (Brasil)



Why Orchestrator.inc

One coding agent can handle a task. Running several means splitting the work, keeping branches from colliding, and following every change through CI, review, and merge. Orchestrator.inc is a local desktop workspace for that: every task gets its own agent, branch, and worktree, and your code stays on your machine.

Features

The orchestrator runs the fleet

Tell a project's main agent what you want built. It plans the work, starts a worker for each piece in its own worktree, and comes back only when something needs you.

One board for every session

Sessions sort themselves into lanes from the agent, its PR, CI, and reviews, so whatever needs you is on top.

CI fails, the right agent fixes it

Failed checks, review comments, and merge conflicts go back to the worker that owns the branch until the PR is approved. A reviewer agent can read every PR before a person does.

Use the agent you already trust

Pick the agent and model per task, then work in structured chat or the agent's own terminal UI. Each worker also gets a browser to preview and test its app.

Supported agents

Worker, Chat, and reviewer support differ by agent; the agent setup guides have the current matrix.

  Claude Code   Codex   Cursor
  opencode   Aider   GitHub Copilot
  Grok   Kimi   Pi
  Amp   Auggie   Droid
  Crush   Cline   Goose
  Qwen   Continue   Devin
  Kiro   Kilo Code   Vibe
  Muse   Agy Autohand
  Kimchi   Prime Agent   OMP
  fx   Unreal Agent   MiMo Code
  Gemini CLI   DeepSeek   OpenCode 2
  Codewhale   Command Code   OpenHands

Orchestrator for Mobile

Control the agents running on your desktop from your phone. Install the app for iPhone or Android. Scan the QR code in Settings → Connect Mobile to pair it with your desktop. It works on your home Wi-Fi and away from home.

  • Get alerts. A push notification tells you when an agent has a question or needs approval.
  • Reply. Answer in chat, approve the request, or open the agent's terminal.
  • Start work. Create a new worker and pick its agent and model.
  • Review. Check pull requests and reviewer results.

Cloud Agents

Run workers in hosted workspaces instead of on your machine. Choose Clone to the cloud and pick a GitHub repository to start.

  • Keep running. Tasks keep going with your laptop closed.
  • Follow along. Open the chat, files, and terminal from the desktop app.
  • Nothing on your machine. The code, worktrees, and agents all live in the cloud.

See the Cloud guide for setup.

Install

Download from orchestrator.inc/download or GitHub Releases. The app updates itself.

Platform Download
macOS (Apple silicon) Orchestrator-darwin-arm64.dmg
macOS (Intel) Orchestrator-darwin-x64.dmg
Windows agent-orchestrator-win32-x64.exe
Linux (AppImage) agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.AppImage
Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.deb
Linux (Fedora/RHEL) agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.rpm

Open Orchestrator.inc and point it at the repository you want it to manage. The desktop app runs the daemon for you, so no CLI is required. See the installation guide for agent CLI setup and troubleshooting.

Documentation

Document Start here when you need
Product documentation Installation, agent setup, and day-to-day product usage.
docs/documentation-map.md Which docs are human-facing, which are machine-readable contracts, and which wins on drift.
docs/architecture.md Backend mental model, lifecycle, persistence, CDC, status derivation, and daemon boundaries.
docs/backend-code-structure.md Package ownership and where each backend concern belongs.
docs/cli/README.md CLI behavior and daemon route mapping.
docs/development.md Prerequisites, build steps, running tests, and troubleshooting for local development.
docs/STATUS.md What currently ships on main and what remains in flight.

Contributing

Start with the development guide for prerequisites, local setup, and test commands. Read CONTRIBUTING.md before opening a pull request, and use GitHub Issues for bugs and feature requests.

Report a bug

Open a bug report from your own GitHub account. A few sentences on what you did and what went wrong are enough; version, OS, and repro steps help if you have them.

A local coding agent can help gather evidence with the bug-triage skill; keep its logs and notes in attachments, and review the draft before submitting it yourself. Please don't have a bot file issues for you.

For help describing a problem, join the bug-triaging channel on Discord. See contribution guidance for more detail.

Community

Join Discord for help and contributor discussion, follow @useOrchestrator for updates, or start a conversation in GitHub Issues.

Star history

Product telemetry

Orchestrator.inc collects limited usage and reliability telemetry, never your code, prompts, agent conversations, or credentials. It includes an installation ID and your GitHub username; if you sign in to AO Cloud it also includes your AO Cloud user ID and the email address of that account, set once as a PostHog person property (never read from git config). Turn it all off in Settings > General > Privacy > Share usage analytics, which covers the desktop, the daemon, and a paired phone. Learn exactly what we collect and how to opt out.

License

Orchestrator.inc is available under the Apache License 2.0.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A comprehensive control plane for orchestrating, supervising, and executing teams of AI coding agents concurrently.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Agent Orchestrator is a robust management platform that coordinates swarms of diverse AI coding agents to complete complex software projects. Rather than relying on a single agent, it allows developers to delegate specific tasks to specialized agents (such as Claude Code or Codex), providing each with its own isolated workspace and feedback loop. The orchestrator tracks the entire lifecycle of a task from initial planning to final pull request merging. It offers a live Kanban board to supervise parallel agent executions, monitor CI runs, and review code changes, effectively functioning as a project manager for an automated AI workforce.
keyFeatures: Multi-agent coordination: Orchestrates fleets of distinct AI models to work in parallel on separate components of a project.
Isolated execution environments: Provisions dedicated workspaces for each agent to prevent conflicts and ensure reproducible builds.
Lifecycle supervision: Tracks agent progress from initial task assignment through coding, testing, and PR creation.
Universal harness support: Integrates seamlessly with over 25 different agent frameworks and CLI tools.
Live Kanban monitoring: Provides a visual dashboard to oversee worker status, review code diffs, and intervene when necessary.

useCases.description: Deploy multiple agents simultaneously to update syntax across hundreds of files in a massive monorepo.

useCases.title: Automated feature development
useCases.description: Assign one agent to write backend API routes while another concurrently develops the corresponding frontend components.

useCases.title: Continuous integration remediation
useCases.description: Automatically dispatch an agent to investigate and resolve failing test suites flagged in the CI pipeline.

useCases.title: Agent performance benchmarking
useCases.description: Run identical tasks across different AI models to compare their speed, accuracy, and code quality.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Engineering managers, platform engineers, and developers managing complex codebases who want to scale their output using AI automation. It requires infrastructure capable of running multiple containerized agents.
